In 53 years of drainage the bog lost 42 cm of peat, about 500 years of growth

In 1956, as the ditches were cut, surveyors drove an iron post through the peat into the clay, its top level with the surface. Today 42 cm of it stands clear. The ditches were blocked in 2009.

The core beside the post holds 4,200 years of peat. At its long-term rate of 0.8 mm a year, the missing 42 cm took about 500 years to form.

The post measures shrinkage and oxidation together; the core cannot separate them.

Illustrative survey · post read in 2026; ages are calibrated radiocarbon mediansPortrait mass · drawn core

Giant planets are 23% of our detections but only 2% of planets

A transit is the shadow a planet casts on its star. A giant dims its star by about one per cent and is almost never missed; an Earth‑size planet dims it a hundred times less, and most go unseen.

Corrected for the planets each size class hides, the order reverses: Earth‑size planets go from 7% of detections to 21% of planets.

Illustrative survey · 2,660 planets around Sun-like stars, orbits under 100 days; corrected by injection–recovery testsSplit claim · slope chart

Next: swap routes between the two depots for 12 weeks, and see whether the fade follows the yard or the route

Northfield packs lose capacity 2.1 times as fast. Its yard is colder and its routes are longer, so the data so far cannot say which matters.

Fade follows the yard
The cause is cold charging: heat Northfield’s charging bays, £1.4 m.
Fade follows the route
The cause is deep discharge: re-block 9 long routes to keep packs above 30%.

16 buses for 12 weeks, capacity checked every 2 weeks. Decision on 4 March 2027.

Illustrative data · battery management logs, 80 buses, last 18 months; fade = % of capacity lost per 10,000 kmClosing experiment · crossover design
